item.title: Israel launches ‘limited counterterrorism’ op after 2 IDF troops killed in West Bank
item.description: In a post on X, the IDF said, "In response to the shooting attack in which 2 IDF soldiers fell, and several others were wounded, the IDF along with other security forces launched a targeted & limited counterterrorism operation in the Hebron area, from which the terrorists had emerged." The military said residents in areas where its forces are operating would be allowed to leave through three designated exit points.
item.dc:creator: RAJEEV SINGH

item.title: Cuba next? Trump hints at 'little stopover' after US warships return from Iran war
item.description: Trump and Rubio have both adopted a hard line towards Cuba's communist government. In May, the two renewed the possibility of US military intervention, with the threat gaining further significance after the Trump administration announced criminal charges against former Cuban leader Raúl Castro. Trump had floated a similar idea earlier this year but had not raised it publicly in recent months.
item.dc:creator: RAJEEV SINGH

item.title: China’s patrolling deviations disturb border: MEA on ITBP DG's face-offs remark
item.description: The ministry of external affairs (MEA) on Friday did not go into the specifics of the latest face-off, choosing to refer the issue to the defence ministry, but said Chinese divergence from established patrolling patterns created disturbances at the border from time to time. The official said both sides continued to use existing diplomatic and military mechanisms to resolve outstanding issues and avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation along the LAC.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: Upper layer NBFCs have to list: RBI guv on Tatas; dispels doubts on Sept order
item.description: RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra’s comments also suggest Tata Sons is in breach of RBI rules. The consequences of continued noncompliance remain unclear. The governor declined to be drawn into the question of Noel Tata’s proposal to merge two Tata Sons subsidiaries with the holding company, a move that could help it sidestep a stock market listing.
item.dc:creator: REEBA ZACHARIAH

item.title: Trump eases tariffs on Canadian imports weeks before US midterms
item.description: The White House said the changes would remove tariffs on certain products, including "plywood sheets, some paper products, certain machinery and refrigeration equipment". However, the administration will also introduce tariffs on other goods, including carpets, certain valves and waste products. The new measures will take effect on October 30. The United States and Canada have closely connected economies.
item.dc:creator: RAJEEV SINGH

item.title: Mark Zuckerberg says Meta's Muse chatbot adoption is strong, but AI may not stay free
item.description: Meta has launched its AI agent Muse, which is already being used by over 10 million people. CEO Mark Zuckerberg indicated that Muse's revenue potential could surpass that of Facebook and Instagram. Currently, shopping is the most common use case for the Muse agent, with consumers spending an average of $200 per purchase.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: New York family loses half its private road to 1,500-member club in court
item.description: In a landmark ruling, a New York family has lost their claim to a shared private road that now belongs to a nearby recreational club. This road, previously amicably used for decades, became contentious in 2021 when disagreements over access arose. The state’s highest court ultimately sided with the club, citing its historical maintenance and usage, despite the family's assertions of permission based on their long-term relationship.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Cabinet Secretary didn’t act on EC’ plaint as it was unofficial: RTI
item.description: According to documents shared as part of an RTI response, two ECs in their separate but near-identical letters to Somanathan on July 29 objected to Garg’s conduct and an order he issued revising allocation of work among senior officers. The two ECs alleged the changes were made without prior discussion with the commission or officers concerned.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: Centre bans reuse of single-use medical devices across hospitals
item.description: In a letter dated Oct 16, the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) said it had come to its notice that some private and corporate hospitals were reusing single-use devices after sterilising them, including items used in cardiology, nephrology, oncology, cardiothoracic and vascular surgery (CTVS), neurosurgery and other clinical services. The DGHS said that reuse could expose patients to cross-infection, device malfunction, reduced performance and other complications.
item.dc:creator: ANUJA JAISWAL

item.title: Two critical PHP flaws trigger global alert; millions of services face cyber risk
item.description: PHP advised users on Oct 23 to temporarily disable its session upload progress feature until the next regular bugfix release. The warning followed an earlier advisory on Oct 21 about a related vulnerability. The latest issue affects applications only when specific session settings are changed while running and the upload progress feature remains enabled. Users who have already disabled the feature do not need to take further action.
item.dc:creator: SHILPA PHADNIS

item.title: Chloë Grace Moretz bought LA home at 19 for $3.4m, sold it for $5.65m
item.description: Chloë Grace Moretz purchased a $3.4 million home in Studio City in 2016 and hosted numerous gatherings there. After seven years, she listed the property for almost $6 million and sold it for $5.65 million. The home features multiple entertainment spaces, a separate studio, and luxurious outdoor areas. Studio City remains a popular area for high-profile buyers, including Olivia Wilde, who sold her property in December 2025.
item.dc:creator: TOI REAL ESTATE DESK

item.title: LA couple bought $925,000 farm, made barn a home, started cider business
item.description: David Bailey and Dana Tiel left their advertising careers to purchase a 16-acre farm in California. After spending $1 million, they converted a barn loft into their home. Their farm, Sierra Cider, includes a petting zoo, pumpkin patch and cider tastings. The couple faced challenges while balancing work and renovations during their transition. Despite initial doubts, the farm has become a popular destination for families and children.
item.dc:creator: TOI REAL ESTATE DESK

item.title: After renaming Lake Ontario, Google CEO rejects US request to rename Atlantic Ocean
item.description: President Trump has recently proposed renaming the Atlantic Ocean, following prior discussions about the Atlantic Ocean. During a recent event, he mentioned contacting Google Maps regarding these renaming efforts. Google CEO Sundar Pichai reportedly declined his proposal on the grounds that oceans encompass multiple countries. This follows the US administration's earlier renaming of Lake Ontario to Lake America for US users.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Cameron Diaz bought LA home for $1.8m, later sold it to Ariana Grande for $4.9m
item.description: Ariana Grande acquired Cameron Diaz's Hollywood Hills property in 2022 through an off-market deal worth $4.9 million. The home features two bedrooms, two-and-a-half bathrooms, and is situated at the end of a cul-de-sac. Cameron Diaz originally bought the house in 2004 for $1.8 million but never lived there. The property underwent many renovations during Diaz's ownership, enhancing its condition before Grande's purchase.
item.dc:creator: TOI REAL ESTATE DESK

item.title: ‘A racist terror attack’: Emmanuel Macron condemns deadly shooting near Paris
item.description: "These people were targeted because of their skin colour or perceived religion, and for no other reason," Macron said after meeting officials and residents in Trappes. "There is no place for this in France." Macron also said the suspect's statements indicated that the attack had been planned in advance. Police arrested the suspect less than 20 minutes after the shooting began.
item.dc:creator: RAJEEV SINGH

item.title: Need to unite against divisive forces, tackle new challenges: PM Modi
item.description: Inaugurating the Chinmaya Amrit Mahotsav Global Sammelan, he said Swami Chinmayananda set his goals as per issues facing the country at the time and new challenges had emerged in the past few decades. “We must unite society against divisive forces. We must inspire citizens toward self-reliance, and we must connect every individual to vision of a developed India by 2047. For these objectives, we must become more proactive,” he said.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: Tom Brady donates $170,000 speaking fee to charity
item.description: Tom Brady collected $170,000 for a speaking gig at Salem State University, generously donating the entire sum to charity. He allocated $50,000 to Best Buddies and distributed the remaining funds to various other organizations. With approximately 4,000 attendees present, ticket sales effectively covered his speaking fee. However, the event was notable for Brady facing questions about the NFL's Deflategate saga. The university reported a financial profit from hosting the event.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: Andy Murray’s wife and four children: Inside his family life after retirement
item.description: Andy Murray has officially retired from professional tennis and, in doing so, has opened a new chapter in his life, and the former world No 1 will have more time to spend with his wife Kim Sears and their four children. From parenting and family routines to their shared business interests at Cromlix, the couple are handling life outside the demands of professional tennis while keeping family at the center.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: Ukrainian soldier cuts off his own foot to survive, rescued by drone after 8 months
item.description: Kostiantyn Vlasenko, 49, had been stranded in a boiler room with severe injuries after a Russian drone strike. With no way to escape and little hope of being rescued, he made a desperate decision to amputate his remaining foot to survive. On October 4, a large drone lifted him into the air using a harness and carried him 15km to safety.
item.dc:creator: RAJEEV SINGH

item.title: Opposition's 'mock Parliament' to step up fight against SIR & CEC Gyanesh Kumar
item.description: Sources said a “mock” gathering depicting an assembly of MPs may take place in the national capital on Oct 28. The event will involve MPs and others, but is unlikely to be a large gathering, given that a massive show of strength to push for the CEC’s resignation is planned at Ramlila Maidan as a “Delhi chalo” rally.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: Arms training case: US mercenary VanDyke, 6 Ukrainians to remain abroad till Feb 24
item.description: VanDyke attended the court hearing Friday and sought the release of his seized personal articles. The seven accused had earlier sought six weeks to meet their families and were allowed to stay abroad till Oct 23. They were arrested on March 13 for allegedly training the insurgent-linked groups in Myanmar.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: Northwest India turned drier, south wetter over 70 years, finds IMD study
item.description: In northwest India, the hot semi-arid zone grew from about a quarter of the region’s area in 1951-1980 to a third in 1991-2020, while the temperate zone shrank from about a quarter to less than a fifth, meaning that an area equal to roughly 7% of the region moved into the drier zone as temperatures rose and rainfall declined, said the study.
item.dc:creator: VISHWA MOHAN

item.title: Brics parliamentary meet should end with joint statement: LS Speaker Om Birla
item.description: Talking to reporters Friday, Birla said the forum in India would work towards consensus-based dialogue on the role of Parliament in strengthening institutions, promotion of human-centred innovation in AI and digital technologies through Parliament, more representative system of global governance and role of Parliament in ensuring a sustainable and inclusive future for Brics countries.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: New norms for cars from 2029: Rear-crash tests, data recorders
item.description: The ministry has set mandatory timelines for automakers to comply with other Automotive Industry Standards (AIS), covering occupant protection in offset frontal and lateral collisions, protection of pedestrians and other vulnerable road users, and fitment of immobilisers. The requirements will come into effect from April 2027 onwards. In a notification, the ministry also made AIS-192 mandatory for Event Data Recorders (EDRs) installed in cars from Oct 2029.
item.dc:creator: DIPAK K DASH

item.title: After Op Sindoor friction, Delhi & Baku reset ties with EAM Jaishankar's visit
item.description: Ties between the two countries had been held back by geopolitical reasons for a while, mainly Azerbaijan’s ties with Pakistan — as evident from its support for Islamabad after Op Sindoor last year — and India’s defence ties with Armenia. While Bayramov spoke about taking the relationship to a higher level, setting aside past differences, Jaishankar underlined the significance of trade and energy cooperation. Terrorism was also discussed.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: Study traces how an El Niño changed the pollution map
item.description: Coming ahead of India’s peak pollution season, the paper, titled ‘Air quality in flux: The baffling ENSO transition in India’, published in Atmospheric Pollution Research journal Thursday, found that La Niña/El Niño conditions altered atmospheric circulation, PM2.5 transport pathways and weather conditions that determine whether pollution disperses or gets trapped.
item.dc:creator: AMITAVA BHATTACHARYA

item.title: 'It's a crime': UP CEO on alteration of 10,470 Pilbhit voters after SIR final roll
item.description: Uttar Pradesh's chief electoral officer revealed that two electoral officials and a computer operator have been implicated in voter record manipulation. A total of 10,470 voter records were altered without any supporting applications found in the offices. The manipulation was discovered after a voter noticed discrepancies in his registration details and reported them. Legal actions include criminal charges and potential disciplinary measures against the officials involved in the case.
item.dc:creator: ARVIND CHAUHAN

item.title: GT player added to India squad as cover for injured Ishan Kishan for second T20I
item.description: Kushagra was part of the India A squad set to face New Zealand A in a three-match unofficial Test series beginning on Saturday in Lincoln. He will now join the senior team for the second T20I at Hagley Oval in Christchurch.
item.dc:creator: SHUBHANSHU DWIVEDI

item.title: 'Nobody knows truth': Akhilesh dismisses seat-sharing figures amid Cong's demand
item.description: Akhilesh Yadav has dismissed rumors regarding the number of seats Congress is requesting for the 2027 elections. Both parties are committed to strengthening their alliance to defeat the BJP. Congress has submitted a list of 175 to 200 constituencies where it believes it can perform well. SP leaders emphasize that seat allocation should be based on winnability rather than political bargaining.
item.dc:creator: ARVIND CHAUHAN

item.title: Bayern Munich coach collapses after training session, taken to hospital
item.description: Bayern sporting director Max Eberl said the club would give Kompany all the time he needed to recover, stressing that his health remained the priority.
item.dc:creator: SHUBHANSHU DWIVEDI

item.title: 5 dead as blast rips through house storing firecrackers in Bihar village
item.description: A significant explosion occurred in Alampur village, leading to the deaths of five individuals. Firecrackers stored in a house ignited, causing widespread panic among local residents. Siwan Superintendent of Police announced the formation of a special team to investigate the incident. Authorities are looking into the licensing and safety practices related to firecracker storage in the area.
item.dc:creator: KSHITIZ

item.title: Netanyahu orders sweeping West Bank offensive after deadly Hebron attack
item.description: In light of a tragic shooting on October 23 that claimed the lives of two soldiers near Hebron, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has initiated preparations for a military operation in the West Bank. This strategy includes imposing movement restrictions on Palestinians and conducting extensive weapon searches. With national elections looming on October 27, Netanyahu's government feels compelled to respond decisively amidst escalating violence and coalition partner pressures.
item.dc:creator: ARYAN SINGH

item.title: Pratika Rawal's ton, Charani's four-for power India to nine-wicket win over Zimbabwe
item.description: Zimbabwe were bowled out for 197 despite a half-century from Beloved Biza, with Charani and Kranti Gaud (3/42) leading India's bowling effort. Pratika then guided the chase with an unbeaten 100 as India reached 200/1 in 27.1 overs to take a 1-0 lead in the series.

item.title: Why PSG stars may miss Ballon d’Or Night as club faces tragic repeat of last year
item.description: A last-minute security-driven postponement of PSG’s Ligue 1 clash against Lyon has created a scheduling conflict with the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony in London. With 10 players nominated, the French champions face a dilemma over balancing club commitments and football’s biggest individual awards. Injured stars, including defending winner Ousmane Dembélé, could have greater freedom to attend, but final plans remain unconfirmed.
item.dc:creator: SOROR SHAIZA

item.title: Kohli ignored calls after promising India comeback: Amit Mishra makes huge claim
item.description: Mishra said the assurances from Kumble and Kohli did not translate into a return to the national team, with the match against England eventually becoming his final international appearance for India.
item.dc:creator: SHUBHANSHU DWIVEDI
